crime: In the lounge, {WITCH_NAME} started letter after letter to her father, and with her Magic unwrote every one back to blank paper.

Every morning it snowed, one of the prisoners stood at the courtyard fountain with a handful of crusts for the birds and called for her to come out. She never did. Then, at dawn after one snowfall, {WITCH_NAME} swept a path out to the girl for the first time. Her father used to sweep a path to her door, but only on the mornings he came home.

At the fountain, the girl tipped the crusts into her hands. "You feed them from tomorrow." Then she turned to go. {WITCH_NAME} slammed the girl's head against the fountain and held her face in the snow until she was still. Back in the doorway, {WITCH_NAME} undid her sweeping, and the snow lay over the path again, untouched, as it had been before she began.

Later that morning, the prisoners found the girl by the fountain with only her own footprints in the snow, and ruled that she had slipped and struck her head on it by herself. Then one prisoner found half a footprint near the body: a heel pressed clearly into the snow, its toes lost under a smooth surface. In the trial court, the prisoners realized that someone had swept a path out to the fountain and then put the snow back, and that only one of them undid her own work like that: the girl who unwrote her letters.
fields.epitaph: She left the snow unbroken behind her, and became the one who never came.
fields.epithet: The Girl in the Doorway, Facing Unbroken Snow
execution: The execution stand straps her on her back at the far end of a long iron trough heaped with snow. An iron broom starts at the other end and sweeps a path toward her, stroke by stroke, and stops one step short. Then the swept snow slides back. It fills the path, runs over her face and packs itself smooth. The surface stirs, then stops, as smooth as if no one had ever swept it.

magic.name: As If Never Begun
magic.text: She can undo anything she has made with her own hands, back to before she began.
